The Cow That Came on Its Own

phrases.sw: Asubuhi moja Anna alitoka nje ya nyumba yake na kuona ng'ombe amesimama mlangoni mwake. Mzuri, wa rangi ya kahawia nyekundu, mtulivu. Ng'ombe alikuwa peke yake — bila kamba, bila mwenyewe, bila maelezo. Anna hakuwa na ng'ombe. Sasa alikuwa naye. Anna alimpa maji na majani. Jioni hakuna aliyekuja kuchukua ng'ombe. Wiki moja baadaye pia hakuna aliyekuja. Majirani walisema: huyu ni ng'ombe wako. Anna hakuwa na uhakika. Lakini maziwa yalikuwa ya kweli.
phrases.en: One morning Anna came out of her house and saw a cow standing at her door. Beautiful, reddish-brown, calm. The cow was alone — no rope, no owner, no explanation. Anna didn't have a cow. Now she did. Anna gave it water and hay. In the evening nobody came for the cow. A week later nobody came either. The neighbours said: this is your cow. Anna was not sure. But the milk was real.

phrases.sw: Grace ana mpwa. Ana miaka saba na anajua kila kitu. Anajua mvua iko wapi, anajua basi litakuja lini, anajua kwa nini jogoo analia saa tisa usiku hasa. Siku moja Grace alimwuliza: nguo yangu ya buluu iko wapi? Alisema: ilikuwa kwenye kamba. Sasa haipo. Lakini itakuwa kwako kesho asubuhi. Asubuhi nguo ilikuwa imelala mlangoni. Yenye unyevu na safi. Nani alileta — haijulikani.
phrases.en: Grace has a nephew. He is seven years old and he knows everything. He knows where the rain is, he knows when the bus will come, he knows why the rooster crows at exactly three in the morning. One day Grace asked him: where is my blue cloth? He said: it was on the line. It is not there now. But it will be with you tomorrow morning. In the morning the cloth was lying at the door. Wet and clean. Who brought it — nobody knows.

phrases.sw: Grace ana mapishi ya siri ya supu aliyoyarithisha kutoka kwa bibi yake. Tatizo ni kwamba kamwe hana viungo vyote vinavyohitajika wakati mmoja. Leo kuna vitunguu lakini hakuna nyama. Jana kulikuwa na nyama lakini haikuwa na vitunguu. Supu itakuwa. Siku moja.
phrases.en: Grace has a secret soup recipe she inherited from her grandmother. The problem is that she never has all the ingredients at the same time. Today there is onion but there is no meat. Yesterday there was meat but there was no onion. The soup will happen. Someday.

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 1. Kitenzi kimoja cha "kuwa" au vingi
moderator_questions.en: Question 1. One verb "to be" or several

body.sw:
Angalia tafsiri zako za aina tatu za sentensi:

- "John ni mwalimu" — ni nani yeye
- "John yuko nyumbani" — yuko wapi
- "John amechoka" — ana hali gani sasa hivi

Katika Kihispania kuna vitenzi viwili tofauti — ser kwa "John ni mwalimu" na estar kwa "John yuko nyumbani" na "John amechoka". Katika Kiswahili pia kuna maneno mawili tofauti — ni kwa utambulisho na yuko kwa mahali.

Katika lugha yako — ni neno moja katika hali zote tatu au maneno tofauti?
body.en:
Look at your translations of three types of phrases:

- "John is a teacher" — who he is
- "John is at home" — where he is
- "John is tired" — what he is like right now

In Spanish these are two different verbs — ser for "John is a teacher" and estar for "John is at home" and "John is tired". In Swahili there are also two different words — ni for identity and yuko for location.

In your language — is it the same word in all three cases or different words?

sw: Neno moja kwa hali zote tatu
Maneno tofauti → mangapi? neno gani kwa hali gani? toa mifano
en: One word for all three cases
Different words → how many? which word for which case? give examples

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 2. Sifa ya kudumu vs hali ya muda
moderator_questions.en: Question 2. Permanent property vs temporary state

body.sw:
Katika Kihispania "John es alto" — John ni mrefu (daima, ni sifa yake) na "John está cansado" — John amechoka (sasa hivi, kwa muda) — vitenzi tofauti.

Katika Kirusi na Kiingereza neno moja linafunika hali zote mbili — "John ni mrefu" na "John amechoka" — hakuna tofauti katika kitenzi.

Angalia tafsiri zako:

- "John ni mwalimu" (kudumu)
- "John amechoka" (sasa hivi)
- "John ana ugonjwa" (kwa muda)
- "John ni mrefu" (daima)

Katika lugha yako — je kuna tofauti ya kisarufi kati ya sifa ya kudumu na hali ya muda?
body.en:
In Spanish "John es alto" — John is tall (always, it is his property) and "John está cansado" — John is tired (right now, temporarily) — these are different verbs.

In Russian and English one word covers both cases — "John is tall" and "John is tired" — no difference in the verb.

Look at your translations:

- "John is a teacher" (permanent)
- "John is tired" (right now)
- "John is sick" (temporary)
- "John is tall" (always)

In your language — is there a grammatical distinction between a permanent property and a temporary state?

sw: Hapana — umbo moja kwa hali zote mbili
Ndiyo — kuna tofauti → inavyoonyeshwa vipi hasa? toa mifano
en: No — one form for both cases
Yes — there is a distinction → how exactly is it expressed? give examples

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 3. Ukanushi wa "kuwa" na "kuwa na"
moderator_questions.en: Question 3. Negation of "to be" and "to have"

body.sw:
Angalia tafsiri zako za sentensi za ukanushi:

- "John si mwalimu"
- "John hayuko nyumbani"
- "Sina kitabu"

Katika baadhi ya lugha ukanushi wa "kuwa" unajengwa kwa njia maalum — si tu kuongeza "si" mbele ya kitenzi. Katika Kiswahili "ni" → "si" — neno tofauti kabisa. Katika Kirusi "у меня есть" → "у меня нет" na nomino inabadilika umbo lake.

Katika lugha yako — ukanushi wa "kuwa" na "kuwa na" unajengwa kama ukanushi wa kawaida au kuna umbo maalum?
body.en:
Look at your translations of the negative phrases:

- "John is not a teacher"
- "John is not at home"
- "I don't have a book"

In some languages negation of "to be" is built in a special way — it is not simply a matter of adding "not" before the verb. In Swahili "ni" → "si" — a completely different word. In Russian "у меня есть" → "у меня нет" and the noun changes its form.

In your language — is the negation of "to be" and "to have" built like regular negation or is there a special form?

sw: Ukanushi wa kawaida — chembe ya ukanushi inaongezwa tu
Umbo maalum kwa "kuwa" → ni lipi? toa mifano
Umbo maalum kwa "kuwa na" → ni lipi? toa mifano
Je nomino inabadilika wakati wa ukanushi wa "kuwa na" → toa mifano
en: Regular negation — a negative particle is simply added
A special form for "to be" → what is it? give examples
A special form for "to have" → what is it? give examples
Does something change in the noun when negating "to have" → give examples

body.sw:
Angalia vikundi hivi viwili vya sentensi:

- "Nina kitabu" — kitabu ni changu
- "Kuna kitabu ndani ya nyumba" — kitabu kipo tu ndani ya nyumba, bila mmiliki

Katika baadhi ya lugha hii ni muundo mmoja. Katika nyingine ni tofauti kabisa.

Katika lugha yako — "nina kitabu" na "kuna kitabu ndani ya nyumba" vinajengwa vivyo hivyo au tofauti?
body.en:
Look at these two groups of phrases:

- "I have a book" — the book belongs to me
- "There is a book in the house" — the book is simply in the house, without an owner

In some languages this is the same construction. In others they are completely different.

In your language — are "I have a book" and "there is a book in the house" built the same way or differently?

sw: Vivyo hivyo — muundo mmoja kwa hali zote mbili
Tofauti → vinatofautiana vipi hasa? toa mifano yote miwili pamoja
en: The same — one construction for both cases
Differently → how exactly do they differ? give both examples side by side

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 5. "Kuwa" katika wakati wa sasa
moderator_questions.en: Question 5. "To be" in the present tense

body.sw:
Katika baadhi ya lugha kitenzi "kuwa" katika wakati wa sasa kinatoweka kabisa — "John ni mwalimu" ni maneno mawili tu bila kitenzi, kama katika Kirusi ya mazungumzo au Kiarabu.

Katika lugha nyingine kitenzi "kuwa" ni lazima daima — kama katika Kiingereza "John is a teacher".

Angalia tafsiri zako za sentensi za wakati wa sasa. Je kuna kitenzi "kuwa" ndani yake au maneno mawili yanasimama tu pamoja bila kitenzi?
body.en:
In some languages the verb "to be" disappears completely in the present tense — "John is a teacher" is simply two words next to each other with no verb, as in colloquial Russian or in Arabic.

In other languages the verb "to be" is always required — as in English "John is a teacher".

Look at your translations of the present tense phrases. Is there a verb "to be" in them or do the two words simply stand next to each other without a verb?

sw: Kitenzi kipo — ni lazima katika wakati wa sasa
Hakuna kitenzi — maneno yanasimama pamoja bila kitenzi
Inategemea aina ya sentensi → eleza katika hali zipi kitenzi kipo na katika zipi hakipo
en: The verb is there — it is required in the present tense
There is no verb — the words stand next to each other without a verb
It depends on the type of phrase → explain in which cases the verb is present and in which it is not

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 6. Kukusanya kitabu cha sarufi

body.sw: Kulingana na maudhui yote yaliyotolewa — tafsiri za sentensi na majibu ya maswali hapo juu — tunga kitabu kifupi cha sarufi kuhusu kitenzi "kuwa" na muundo "kuwa na" katika lugha yako.
body.en: Based on all the content provided — translations of phrases and answers to the questions above — write a short grammar reference on the verb "to be" and the construction "to have" in your language.

sw: Kitenzi "kuwa" — je kipo, je kinabadilika kwa nafsi, neno moja au vingi
Utambulisho, mahali, hali — vivyo hivyo au maumbo tofauti
Sifa ya kudumu vs hali ya muda — je kuna tofauti
"Kuwa" katika wakati wa kale na kesho — jinsi inavyobadilika
Ukanushi wa "kuwa" — jinsi unavyojengwa
Umiliki — kitenzi "kuwa na" au muundo mwingine
Ukanushi wa umiliki — jinsi unavyojengwa, je nomino inabadilika
Uwepo bila mmiliki — sawa na umiliki au tofauti
Mifano ya sentensi kwa kila kanuni
en: The verb "to be" — does it exist, does it change by person, one word or several
Identity, location, state — the same or different forms
Permanent property vs temporary state — is there a distinction
"To be" in the past and future — how it changes
Negation of "to be" — how it is built
Possession — verb "to have" or construction "I have"
Negation of possession — how it is built, does the noun change
Existence without an owner — the same as possession or different
Example sentences for each rule
